tasks.title: Create Epic records and read APIs
tasks.description: Implement persisted Epic records with title, description, priority, active status, and timestamps, then expose create, list, and show operations through the backend service and HTTP API. List and show responses should include a progress object that returns zero delivered and zero total for Epics without linked issues.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an Epic with title, description, and priority persists an active Epic and returns its id
Listing Epics returns status, priority, description summary data, and projected progress for each Epic
Showing an Epic returns the full description, status, priority, linked issue array, and projected progress
Invalid create input returns a structured validation error
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/src/db and packages/cli/src/api Epic create/list/show support
tasks.notes: Creates the persisted Epic base needed by later membership, UI, and CLI tasks.

tasks.title: Link issues to Epics with projected progress
tasks.description: Implement primary Epic membership so users can add and remove existing issues from an Epic while enforcing that an issue belongs to at most one Epic. Update Epic detail/list projection to derive delivered count, total count, blocked issues, active issues, and next issue from linked issue state using the required priority order.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding an existing issue to an existing Epic makes it appear in Epic detail linked issues
Removing a linked issue removes only the Epic membership and does not change issue workflow state
Adding an issue that already belongs to another Epic fails with a clear structured error that identifies the existing Epic
Epic progress derives deliveredCount and totalIssueCount from linked issues on read
Epic nextIssue chooses a blocked issue first, then an active issue, then a backlog issue, otherwise returns ready-to-mark-done state
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/src/services Epic membership and progress projection
tasks.notes: Keep Progress as read-time projection, not a persisted entity.

tasks.title: Expose Epic lifecycle actions
tasks.description: Add explicit lifecycle operations that let users mark an Epic done or close it without changing linked issues or triggering workflow execution. The backend API should expose lifecycle verbs and reject unsupported workflow-style operations for Epics by absence rather than by adding Epic rows to issue workflow paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Marking an active Epic done changes only the Epic status to done
Closing an Epic changes only the Epic status to closed
Done and closed lifecycle actions do not modify linked issue status, stage, worktree, or run data
No API route or command path starts workflow execution for an Epic
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/src/api Epic done and close endpoints
tasks.notes: Expose both done and close because Web behavior requires done and CLI acceptance requires close.

tasks.title: Return primary Epic on issue detail
tasks.description: Extend issue detail data so a single issue can report its primary Epic summary when one exists. The response should be sufficient for clients to render a backlink without client-side searching or widening Board lane data.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue detail for a linked issue includes the primary Epic id, title, status, and priority
Issue detail for an unlinked issue clearly reports no primary Epic
Issue list and Board lane responses are not changed to include Epic rows as workflow items
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/src/api issue detail primaryEpic response data
tasks.notes: Prefer extending only the existing issue detail shape used by the detail page.

tasks.title: Add Epic list and create Web UI
tasks.description: Add an Epics navigation surface and Web UI for listing active/done/closed Epics and creating a new Epic with title, description, and priority. The list should show status, delivered/total progress, and the projected next issue from the backend response.
acceptanceCriteria: Main navigation includes Epics without adding Epics to Board lanes
Users can create an Epic from the Web UI using title, description, and priority
Epic list groups or distinguishes active, done, and closed Epics
Each listed Epic shows delivered/total progress and backend-provided next issue or ready-to-mark-done state
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/web/src Epic navigation, list, and create UI
tasks.notes: Keep create form limited to title, description, and priority.

tasks.title: Add Epic detail management Web UI
tasks.description: Implement the Epic detail work surface showing description, status, priority, progress, next issue, and linked issues. Add controls to link an existing issue by id, remove a linked issue, mark done, and close the Epic while surfacing duplicate-membership errors clearly.
acceptanceCriteria: Epic detail shows description, delivered/total progress, next issue, and all linked issues with their current issue states
Users can add an existing issue to the Epic from the detail page
Users can remove a linked issue from the Epic detail page
Duplicate issue membership errors are displayed with a clear explanation instead of a generic failure
Users can mark an Epic done or close it from the detail page
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/web/src Epic detail and membership UI
tasks.notes: Use backend progress projection directly; do not reimplement next-issue rules in React.

tasks.title: Add Issue detail Epic backlink Web UI
tasks.description: Render a compact primary Epic backlink on the Issue Detail page when the issue belongs to an Epic. The link should route users back to the Epic detail page and stay hidden for unlinked issues.
acceptanceCriteria: Linked issue detail renders `Part of Epic` with Epic id and title
Clicking the Epic backlink opens the corresponding Epic detail page
Unlinked issue detail does not render an empty or misleading Epic backlink
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/web/src Issue detail primary Epic backlink
tasks.notes: This should consume issue detail data rather than querying every Epic client-side.

tasks.title: Add Epic CLI commands
tasks.description: Add the `mo epic` command group as a thin server-backed client for creating, listing, showing, adding issues, removing issues, marking done, and closing Epics. CLI output should present status, progress, next issue, and duplicate-membership errors using the same backend semantics as the Web UI.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo epic create` creates an Epic with title, description, and priority through the API client
`mo epic list` shows Epic status, delivered/total progress, and next issue
`mo epic show <id>` shows description, progress, next issue, and linked issues
`mo epic add-issue <epic-id> <issue-id>` and `mo epic remove-issue <epic-id> <issue-id>` manage membership through the API client
`mo epic done <id>` and `mo epic close <id>` update only Epic status
Duplicate membership and not-found failures produce readable CLI errors
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Use the existing shared API client pattern; do not read SQLite directly from CLI commands.

tasks.title: Add Epic regression coverage
tasks.description: Add focused automated coverage for Epic persistence, membership uniqueness, progress projection, API behavior, Web-facing issue backlink data, CLI command mapping, and workflow isolation. The tests should prove Epics remain collections of issues and never become executable workflow items.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover creating, listing, and showing Epics with projected progress
Tests cover duplicate primary Epic membership rejection with a clear error
Tests cover next issue ordering: blocked, active, backlog, then ready-to-mark-done
Tests cover done and close lifecycle actions without linked issue mutation
Tests cover issue detail primary Epic data for linked and unlinked issues
Tests or existing assertions prove Epics do not appear in Board lanes and cannot be started
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Prefer focused service/API tests where UI automation would be brittle.
